rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the priority is to establish a simple, low-cost reference point before testing more complex encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion. config_001 tests whether RNA alone with a basic PCA representation and a single profile provides useful predictive signal. This isolates the RNA-only baseline and creates an anchor for later comparisons of RNA encoders, profile settings, and multimodal designs, making it a strong first experiment under a limited budget.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with moderate accuracy (0.485) and F1 (0.464), leaving major uncertainty about whether image data is informative. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the contribution of the image modality without fusion, aggregation, or multiprofile complexity. This is the best next experiment because it establishes whether image features are useful before spending limited budget on more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is currently the strongest result (0.485 acc) compared with image-only ResNet50 (0.208 acc), so the next step should exploit the RNA direction while testing a major untested design choice. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and model setting as the best baseline but changes to multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile aggregation without introducing a new encoder or fusion. This is the simplest informative test of whether multiprofile RNA aggregation can improve over the singleprofile baseline before investing in more complex transformer, scVI/scGPT, or multimodal variants.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA singleprofile is weak (0.485 acc), while RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool is the strongest result so far (0.591 acc, 0.573 F1). The remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool under the same RNA multiprofile setting. config_003 tests this with a minimal controlled change from config_002, isolating the effect of aggregation. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the currently most promising direction, may yield immediate performance gains, and clarifies whether a more expressive aggregation is worthwhile before moving to multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet singleprofile is weak (0.208 accuracy). This leaves uncertainty about whether image features can add value when fused with the best RNA representation. config_018 keeps the proven RNA PCA/multiprofile/avgpool settings and adds ResNet with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion improves over the RNA-only baseline. It is a focused extension of the current best direction and creates a useful baseline for later fusion or image-encoder comparisons under a limited budget.

The best result so far is config_018, where multiprofile RNA with avgpool, ResNet50 image features, and concat fusion gives the highest accuracy and F1, while image alone is weak and transformer aggregation was less helpful than avgpool. The main untested choice in this promising pipeline is the RNA encoder, since only PCA has been evaluated. config_030 tests whether replacing PCA with a learned scVI RNA representation improves the current best multimodal setting while keeping profile, aggregation, image encoder, and fusion fixed. This is a one-variable extension of the best configuration, balances exploitation of the current best pipeline with exploration of a potentially important representation choice, and may directly yield a better configuration if scVI is more informative than PCA.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile avgpool RNA with PCA is strong (0.591), multimodal concat with resnet50 improves it to 0.619, and replacing PCA with scVI in that multimodal setting gives a small accuracy gain (0.632) but slightly lower F1, so the value of scVI is not yet isolated. config_005 tests scVI in the same RNA-only multiprofile avgpool setting as config_002, changing only the RNA encoder. This clarifies whether the RNA representation itself improves over PCA or whether the multimodal scVI gain is due to interaction or noise, and it also indicates how much image fusion is contributing. Under limited budget, this single-factor RNA-only experiment reduces uncertainty about a key representation decision before committing further to scVI multimodal variants.

The strongest result is RNA-only scvi multiprofile avgpool (config_005, 0.650 acc), while multimodal scvi with ResNet50 avgpool concat (config_030, 0.632 acc) is close but slightly worse, and image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208 acc). This suggests the current multimodal result may be limited by the image representation rather than by multimodality itself. config_036 tests this by replacing ResNet50 with ImageNet ViT-L while keeping the otherwise successful scvi multiprofile avgpool concat setup fixed. It isolates the image encoder effect and clarifies whether a stronger image representation can make multimodal profiling beat the current RNA-only best, which is a high-value uncertainty under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is config_036, which uses scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, imagenet_vit_l, and concat fusion, achieving the best validation accuracy and F1. All completed multimodal experiments used concat, so fusion type remains an untested but important design choice. config_037 keeps the best-known representation, profile setting, and aggregation fixed while changing only fusion to weighted, directly testing whether weighted fusion can improve on concat or whether concat is already sufficient. This is a high-value, one-factor exploitation of the current best direction and is more informative than changing multiple components at once.

The strongest evidence so far is config_036 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + avgpool + concat), with config_037 showing concat slightly outperforming weighted fusion. The remaining important uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool in this best-performing multimodal setup; prior avgpool-vs-transformer evidence is limited to PCA RNA-only and may not transfer to scvi/ViT. config_038 changes only aggregation relative to the current best, cleanly isolating that effect while exploiting the strongest known representation and fusion choice.
